analyst_view.overall: Early view: second against first. Castellón have conceded one goal in five home games under Pablo Hernández and have a game in hand, while leaders Almería have not lost in the league since their first two games under García Pimienta. Both sides' current bans (Orozco, Marcos Luna) should be served in round 14, and Castellón may also have their postponed home game with Eibar rescheduled around this date.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, which looks high. I lean lower: Castellón's home record is 12 scored and only one conceded, Almería's away games have averaged two goals, and top-of-the-table meetings tend to be cautious.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners. Almería take few corners away (two at Girona, three at Eibar) but Castellón at home should make up for that, so I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.8 cards. The stakes are high and Castellón were angry about refereeing at Burgos, but Almería have been disciplined in recent away games (two or three yellows), so I stay near the site's number.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.5 shots. Almería's recent away games had 26 and 30 shots in total, and Castellón create plenty at home, so the number looks reasonable.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target. I lean lower: Castellón allow almost nothing at home, and Almería put only three on target at Girona and one at Eibar.
